title: George III: The Real Story of the “Mad King”
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 哈喽，哈喽，哈喽，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 推出的英语学习播客《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上光怪陆离、奇妙有趣的事物，同时还能提升你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to talk about George III, the British king known to history as the Mad King.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要聊聊 George III，也就是历史上面目为人熟知的“疯王”。

sentences.en: But as we will discover, the story is a great deal more complicated than that label suggests.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们将要了解到的那样，事实远比这个标签所暗示的要复杂得多。

sentences.en: OK, let's not waste a minute, and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们废话不多说，马上切入正题。

sentences.en: It is October 1788. At Windsor Castle, the King of Great Britain is behaving strangely.
sentences.zh: 那是 1788 年 10 月。在大不列颠的温莎城堡里，大不列颠国王的行为举止有些反常。

sentences.en: He is talking without stopping. For hours.
sentences.zh: 他喋喋不休地说话。一说就是几个小时。

sentences.en: Sometimes through the night. His words make no sense.
sentences.zh: 有时甚至通宵达旦。他的话语毫无逻辑。

sentences.en: He speaks to people who are not in the room.
sentences.zh: 他在跟一个并不在房间里的人说话。

sentences.en: He wanders the corridors of the castle in the early hours, agitated and incoherent.
sentences.zh: 他大清早地在城堡走廊里徘徊，神情激动，语无伦次。

sentences.en: Then, one afternoon, he walks up to an oak tree, takes hold of its branches, and begins a conversation with it.
sentences.zh: 接着，在一个下午，他走到一棵橡树前，抓起树枝，开始跟它对话。

sentences.en: He is apparently under the impression that he is speaking with the King of Prussia.
sentences.zh: 他显然以为自己正在和普鲁士国王交谈。

sentences.en: His courtiers do not know what to do.
sentences.zh: 他的朝臣们不知所措。

sentences.en: The King, King George III, appears to be going mad.
sentences.zh: 国王，也就是 George III 国王，似乎疯了。

sentences.en: Now, if you know anything about George III, it is probably that he was the Mad King.
sentences.zh: 如果你对 George III 有所了解，那大概就知道他是个“疯王”。

sentences.en: The one who lost America. The one in the musical Hamilton, as a comic, petulant villain who sings about how the colonists will come crawling back to him.
sentences.zh: 那个丢了美洲的人。那个在音乐剧《Hamilton》里出场的人，是一个滑稽、任性的反派，唱着殖民者会如何摇尾乞怜地回到他身边。

sentences.en: The one who ended his days raving in a locked room at Windsor Castle.
sentences.zh: 那个在温莎城堡一间反锁的房间里，神志不清地度过残生的人。

sentences.en: All of that might be true. But it is far from the whole story.
sentences.zh: 所有这些也许都是真的。但这远非事情的全貌。

sentences.en: Because for most of his sixty-year reign, the longest of any male British monarch in history, George III was a serious, devoted, rather ordinary man who just so happened to be a king.
sentences.zh: 因为在他长达六十年的统治期间——这是英国历史上所有男君主中最长的统治期——George III 的绝大多数时间里都是一个严肃、敬业、相当平凡的人，只不过恰好当了国王。

sentences.en: A man who woke up before dawn to check on his crops.
sentences.zh: 一个日出前就醒来查看庄稼的男人。

sentences.en: Who wrote articles about farming under a fake name.
sentences.zh: 一个用化名撰写农业文章的人。

sentences.en: Who was unusually devoted to his wife. In today's episode, we are going to try to set the "mad king" label aside for a moment and look at the full picture.
sentences.zh: 一个对妻子异常专一的人。在今天的节目中，我们将试着暂时抛开“疯王”这个标签，来看看全貌。

sentences.en: We'll start with who George really was before his illness.
sentences.zh: 我们从 George 生病前的真实样貌讲起。

sentences.en: We'll look at the turbulent kingdom he was theoretically the head of.
sentences.zh: 我们来看看他名义上作为元首的那个动荡不安的王国。

sentences.en: We'll look at his illness, and the treatments that were almost certainly making him worse.
sentences.zh: 我们来看看他的病情，以及那些几乎肯定让他病情加重的治疗方法。

sentences.en: And we'll end with a question that historians and doctors are still arguing about today: what was actually wrong with him?
sentences.zh: 最后，我们要探讨一个历史学家和医生至今仍在争论的问题：他到底得了什么病？

sentences.en: So, George III was born in 1738. As the name suggests, he was the third king called George; the other two were his great-grandfather, George I, and his grandfather, George II.
sentences.zh: 那么，George III 出生于 1738 年。顾名思义，他是第三个叫 George 的国王；另外两个是他的曾祖父 George I 和祖父 George II。

sentences.en: And compared to the Georges that came before him, he was something of a fresh start.
sentences.zh: 跟之前的几位 George 相比，他算是一个全新的开始。

sentences.en: The two other Georges were both German, essentially, from the House of Hanover.
sentences.zh: 另外两位 George 基本上都是德国人，来自汉诺威王朝。

sentences.en: Neither could really speak much English, and they had never bothered to learn.
sentences.zh: 两人其实都不会说太多英语，而且也懒得去学。

sentences.en: George III was different. He had been born in London, educated in Britain, and was determined to present himself not as a German prince who happened to wear the British crown, but as a British king.
sentences.zh: George III 则不同。他在伦敦出生，在英国长大，他决心不把自己表现为一个碰巧戴着英国王冠的德国亲王，而是把自己当作一个英国国王。

sentences.en: He was also unlike most other kings. While many European monarchs were flamboyant, extravagant, obsessed with courts and ceremony and mistresses, George was frugal and hardworking.
sentences.zh: 他也跟大多数其他国王不同。许多欧洲君主生活奢靡、铺张浪费，痴迷于宫廷礼仪和情妇，而 George 则节俭且勤奋。

sentences.en: He got up early. He ate simply. He loved his wife.
sentences.zh: 他起得很早。他饮食简单。他深爱着他的妻子。

sentences.en: He had fifteen children with her, and by most accounts, he loved his children too.
sentences.zh: 他和她育有十五个孩子，据大多数记载，他也深爱着他的孩子们。

sentences.en: He was the first British king to be formally educated in the sciences.
sentences.zh: 他是第一位接受过正规科学教育的英国国王。

sentences.en: He had his own astronomical observatory.
sentences.zh: 他有自己的天文台。

sentences.en: He collected maps. He collected clocks. He had an enormous personal library that, after his death, was donated to what became the British Library: 65,000 volumes.
sentences.zh: 他收集地图。他收集时钟。他拥有庞大的个人图书馆，在他死后被捐赠给了日后的英国国家图书馆：藏书量达 65,000 册。

sentences.en: But his real passion was agriculture.
sentences.zh: 但他真正的热情所在是农业。

sentences.en: Under the pen name Ralph Robinson, he wrote articles about farming methods for a publication called the Annals of Agriculture.
sentences.zh: 他以笔名 Ralph Robinson 在一份名为《农业年鉴》的刊物上撰写关于耕作方法的文章。

sentences.en: His readers had no idea they were reading dispatches from the King of Great Britain.
sentences.zh: 他的读者根本不知道他们读的是大不列颠国王发出的消息。

sentences.en: And it wasn't just theory, either. As the expression goes, he was more than happy to get his hands dirty, to roll up his sleeves and do the physical work himself, rather than leave it to others.
sentences.zh: 而且这不仅仅是纸上谈兵。套用一句俗语，他非常乐意弄脏双手，卷起袖子亲自干体力活，而不是把这些留给别人。

sentences.en: He kept a working farm at Windsor. He went out before dawn to check on his livestock.
sentences.zh: 他在温莎经营着一个农场。他天不亮就出去查看牲畜。

sentences.en: He would walk his own fields and sometimes engage in conversation with labourers who would assume he was just another farmer, and would chat away happily about crops and prices and the weather, never guessing who they were talking to.
sentences.zh: 他会亲自巡视田地，有时还会和劳工们攀谈，劳工们会以为他只是另一个普通农户，于是开开心心地聊着庄稼、价格和天气，全然不知他们正在和谁说话。

sentences.en: This was where the nickname came from: Farmer George.
sentences.zh: 他的绰号“农民 George”就是这么来的。

sentences.en: It was meant, by some, as a mockery. The implication was that he was too simple, too earthy, too undignified to be a real king.
sentences.zh: 在某些人看来，这是一种嘲讽。其潜台词是，他太单纯、太接地气、太没有尊严，不配做一个真正的国王。

sentences.en: But the British public, apparently, rather liked it.
sentences.zh: 但英国公众显然还挺喜欢这个绰号。

sentences.en: A king who knew the price of wheat, who went to bed at a reasonable hour, who had not been caught in any scandalous affairs.
sentences.zh: 一个知道小麦价格、按时上床睡觉、没有卷入任何桃色绯闻的国王。

sentences.en: That was a king you could trust. He had other qualities too.
sentences.zh: 那才是一个你可以信任的国王。他还有其他品质。

sentences.en: He was devoted to his wife, and a loyal husband.
sentences.zh: 他深爱妻子，是个忠诚的丈夫。

sentences.en: It was not a love marriage, as the term goes: it was an arranged marriage, a political match.
sentences.zh: 正如这个词所说，这不是一场恋爱婚姻：这是一桩包办婚姻，是一场政治联姻。

sentences.en: She was a German princess, he was an unmarried king.
sentences.zh: 她是一个德国公主，而他是一个未婚的国王。

sentences.en: And they were both incredibly young. She arrived in England, met George the following day and married him the very same evening.
sentences.zh: 而且他们都年轻得难以置信。她抵达英国，第二天就见到了 George，并在当晚和他结了婚。

sentences.en: She was seventeen. He was twenty-two. These things rarely went well.
sentences.zh: 她十七岁。他二十二岁。这种事情很少有好结果的。

sentences.en: But this one did. By all accounts, George adored her, and was faithful to her for their 57-year union.
sentences.zh: 但这桩婚姻却很美满。据各方记载，George 深爱着她，并在长达 57 年的婚姻中对她忠贞不渝。

sentences.en: He bought her a house, a place called the Queen's House, which he had enlarged and redecorated specially for her.
sentences.zh: 他给她买了一座房子，一个被称为“王后官邸”的地方，并专门为她进行了扩建和重新装修。

sentences.en: You can visit it today, and perhaps you have.
sentences.zh: 你今天还可以去参观它，也许你已经去过了。

sentences.en: You might know it by its later name: Buckingham Palace.
sentences.zh: 你可能通过它的另一个名字知道它：白金汉宫。

sentences.en: He was, in short, a dutiful, domestic and decent man, someone who might have lived a quieter and happier life had he not been born in line to the throne.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，他是一个顺从、顾家且正派的人，如果不是生在王位继承序列中，他本可以过上更平静、更幸福的生活。

sentences.en: So, this is the man who became known as the Mad King.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是那个被称为“疯王”的人。

sentences.en: A farmer. A husband. A father. An avid reader.
sentences.zh: 一个农民。一个丈夫。一个父亲。一个狂热的读者。

sentences.en: A man who loved clocks. Not the monster he is sometimes portrayed as.
sentences.zh: 一个热爱时钟的男人。而不是有时被描绘成的那种怪物。

sentences.en: Now, some monarchs are remembered in the history books for their cunning and intelligence, their ability to navigate international politics, manage internal unrest, and leave the country in a stronger position than how they found it.
sentences.zh: 有些君主在历史书上因其狡猾和智慧而被铭记，他们能够驾驭国际政治、处理国内动荡，并使国家处于比他们接手时更强大的位置。

sentences.en: George III might have been a perfectly decent man in many respects, but he was not one of these monarchs.
sentences.zh: George III 在许多方面可能是一个非常正派的人，但他并不是这样的君主。

sentences.en: And it just so happened that he was landed with a series of incredibly tricky problems to deal with.
sentences.zh: 而且碰巧的是，他接手了一系列极其棘手的问题需要处理。

sentences.en: Not immediately, I should say; when he became king, in 1760, things were looking pretty good for Britain.
sentences.zh: 我得说，不是立刻；当他在 1760 年成为国王时，英国的局势看起来相当不错。

sentences.en: Shortly afterwards, the country emerged victorious from the Seven Years War, winning Britain vast new territories across North America, India, and the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 此后不久，该国在七年战争中大获全胜，为英国赢得了横跨北美、印度和加勒比海的辽阔新领土。

sentences.en: But this victory was a double-edged sword.
sentences.zh: 但这场胜利是一把双刃剑。

sentences.en: The country was drowning in debt, and George was now responsible for a vast, difficult-to-govern empire across the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 国家深陷债务泥潭，而 George 现在要为一个庞大且难以治理的大西洋彼岸帝国负责。

sentences.en: And then, within fifteen years, this empire had started to fracture.
sentences.zh: 然后，在十五年内，这个帝国开始分裂。

sentences.en: The American colonies had been growing increasingly restless.
sentences.zh: 美洲殖民地越来越不安分。

sentences.en: Taxation without representation. Trade restrictions.
sentences.zh: 无代表不纳税。贸易限制。

sentences.en: A growing sense that London was governing people it did not understand and did not particularly care about.
sentences.zh: 一种越来越强烈的感觉是，伦敦正在统治那些它并不理解、也并非特别关心的人民。

sentences.en: George and his ministers did not handle the situation well.
sentences.zh: George 和他的大臣们并没有处理好这个局面。

sentences.en: Reforms were proposed and then reversed.
sentences.zh: 改革被提出，然后又被取消。

sentences.en: Taxes were imposed, dropped, and then reimposed.
sentences.zh: 税收被强征、取消，然后又被重新强征。

sentences.en: The colonists were given every reason to stop trusting the intentions of the British Parliament.
sentences.zh: 殖民地有充分的理由不再信任英国议会的意图。

sentences.en: And what came next, well, it came pretty quickly.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的事，嗯，来得相当快。

sentences.en: By 1775, it was war. By 1783, it was over.
sentences.zh: 到 1775 年，战争爆发了。到 1783 年，战争结束了。

sentences.en: Britain had lost.
sentences.zh: 英国输了。

sentences.en: George III is often cast as the villain of this story, at least in the American popular memory.
sentences.zh: 至少在美国大众的记忆中，George III 经常被塑造成这个故事中的反派。

sentences.en: The reality is a little more complicated.
sentences.zh: 现实要复杂一些。

sentences.en: George was a constitutional monarch, not an absolute one.
sentences.zh: George 是一个立宪君主，而不是绝对君主。

sentences.en: In other words, he could influence policy, but it was the British Parliament that ultimately called the shots, that did the real decision-making.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他可以影响政策，但最终拍板、做出真正决策的是英国议会。

sentences.en: He was stubborn, certainly; he resisted American independence for longer than was sensible.
sentences.zh: 他的确很固执；他抵抗美洲独立的时间比理智的做法要长。

sentences.en: And he was not a mere helpless spectator.
sentences.zh: 他也不是一个无助的旁观者。

sentences.en: But he was not single-handedly responsible for the decisions that led to revolution, and ultimately, American independence.
sentences.zh: 但他并非导致革命以及最终美洲独立的那些决策的唯一负责人。

sentences.en: What the loss of America did, undeniably, was wound him.
sentences.zh: 美洲的丧失，无可否认地伤害了他。

sentences.en: He took it personally. He felt it as a failure.
sentences.zh: 他把它当成了个人问题。他觉得这是一次失败。

sentences.en: He even wrote a draft letter of abdication, where he would step down from the throne, before deciding to stay.
sentences.zh: 他甚至写了一份退位诏书草稿，打算从王位上退下来，但最终决定留下来。

sentences.en: And then the French Revolution began. Napoleon appeared.
sentences.zh: 接着法国大革命爆发了。拿破仑出现了。

sentences.en: Britain found itself in almost constant war with France for the best part of twenty years.
sentences.zh: 英国发现自己与法国陷入了长达近二十年的几乎不间断的战争中。

sentences.en: George III, Farmer George, he was not cut out for this.
sentences.zh: George III，农民 George，他可不是干这个的料。

sentences.en: He was a quiet man who wanted to grow turnips and read about astronomy, and there he was, presiding over one of the most violent and consequential periods in modern history.
sentences.zh: 他是一个只想种芜菁、读天文学的安静男人，而他却偏偏主持了现代历史上最暴力、影响最深远的时期之一。

sentences.en: The pressure was relentless. And in the autumn of 1788, when he was fifty years old, something broke.
sentences.zh: 压力挥之不去。在 1788 年的秋天，当他五十岁的时候，有什么东西崩溃了。

sentences.en: The first serious episode begins in October 1788.
sentences.zh: 第一次严重的发作始于 1788 年 10 月。

sentences.en: The symptoms arrive quickly. He becomes agitated and cannot sleep.
sentences.zh: 症状来得很快。他变得焦躁不安，无法入睡。

sentences.en: He talks without stopping, for hours, sometimes through the night, the words tumbling over each other until they lose their meaning.
sentences.zh: 他喋喋不休地说话，一说就是几个小时，有时甚至通宵达旦，话语接连不断，直到失去意义。

sentences.en: He sees and speaks to people who are not there.
sentences.zh: 他看到并对那些并不存在的人说话。

sentences.en: He shakes the branches of an oak tree in Windsor Great Park, apparently believing himself to be in conversation with the King of Prussia.
sentences.zh: 他摇晃着温莎大公园里一棵橡树的树枝，显然认为自己正在与普鲁士国王交谈。

sentences.en: His household is terrified. Charlotte, his wife, is terrified.
sentences.zh: 他的家人们惊恐万分。他的妻子夏洛特惊恐万分。

sentences.en: Doctors are called. And this is where the story takes a dark turn..
sentences.zh: 医生被请来了。而故事也正是在这里转向了黑暗……

sentences.en: The year is 1788. Nobody understands mental illness.
sentences.zh: 那是 1788 年。没有人理解精神疾病。

sentences.en: There is no real vocabulary for it, no framework, and certainly no treatment that could do anything useful.
sentences.zh: 没有真正的词汇来形容它，没有框架，更没有什么治疗方法能起到什么真正有用的作用。

sentences.en: What doctors had instead was a set of interventions built on theories about the body that were already centuries out of date.
sentences.zh: 相反，医生们使用的一套干预措施，是建立在那些已经落后了几个世纪的身体理论之上的。

sentences.en: George's regular physicians have no idea what to do.
sentences.zh: George 的御医们束手无策。

sentences.en: They start by bleeding him. They give him laxatives and emetics, medicines designed to make him vomit.
sentences.zh: 他们首先给他放血。他们给他吃泻药和催吐剂，这些药物旨在让他呕吐。

sentences.en: They apply what were called blistering agents to his legs: caustic chemicals that raise painful blisters on the skin, in the belief that whatever is wrong inside might somehow exit through the wound.
sentences.zh: 他们在他的腿上敷上所谓的起泡剂：能让皮肤起痛苦水泡的腐蚀性化学物质，他们认为体内的任何毛病都可以通过伤口以某种方式排出来。

sentences.en: This is mainstream medical practice in 1788.
sentences.zh: 这是 1788 年的主流医疗实践。

sentences.en: And you don't have to have a medical degree to guess that none of this does any good.
sentences.zh: 你不需要有医学学位也能猜到，这些做法毫无益处。

sentences.en: After several weeks, a specialist is brought in.
sentences.zh: 几个星期后，请来了一位专家。

sentences.en: His name is Francis Willis. He is an unusual figure, a clergyman as well as a physician, but he has a reputation for treating the mentally ill.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫 Francis Willis。他是一个不同寻常的人物，既是神职人员又是医生，但他以治疗精神病患者而闻名。

sentences.en: Parliament is desperate for the king to recover and is willing to try anything.
sentences.zh: 议会迫切希望国王康复，愿意尝试任何方法。

sentences.en: Willis believes that mental illness is caused by what he calls over-excitement.
sentences.zh: Willis 认为精神疾病是由他所谓的过度兴奋引起的。

sentences.en: The cure is control. His method is simple, and it is brutal.
sentences.zh: 治愈的方法是控制。他的方法很简单，也很残酷。

sentences.en: When the king falls into one of these episodes, when he shouts or attacks the attendants around him or becomes impossible to manage, Willis orders for him to be put into a straitjacket, those jackets where your arms are tied down securely around your body so you cannot move, the ones that are sometimes used for violent prisoners.
sentences.zh: 当国王陷入这些发作之一、当他大喊大叫或攻击身边的侍从或者变得无法管教时，Willis 命令把他穿上束衣，就是那种把你的手臂牢牢绑在身体两侧让你无法动弹的衣服，有时用于暴力囚犯的那种。

sentences.en: He is left in it, thrashing and shouting, until he exhausts himself and goes quiet.
sentences.zh: 他被留在束衣里，挣扎着、大喊大叫，直到筋疲力尽、安静下来。

sentences.en: When he is calm, he is rewarded. He is allowed to see Charlotte and the children.
sentences.zh: 当他平静下来时，他会得到奖励。他被允许见夏洛特和孩子们。

sentences.en: He is permitted small comforts. When he becomes difficult again, back into the jacket it is.
sentences.zh: 他被允许享受一些小的安慰。当他再次变得难以对付时，就又得穿上束衣。

sentences.en: Willis also chains the king to his chair when he deems it necessary.
sentences.zh: Willis 还认为必要时将国王用链子锁在椅子上。

sentences.en: When the talking becomes uncontrollable, he has him gagged, a cloth put around his mouth so he cannot talk.
sentences.zh: 当国王说话不受控制时，他会让人塞住他的嘴，用布蒙住他的嘴，这样他就说不出话来了。

sentences.en: The King of Great Britain, monarch of one of the most powerful states in the world, is being managed like a dangerous animal.
sentences.zh: 这位大不列颠国王、世界上最强大国家的君主，正像危险动物一样被对待。

sentences.en: The grim irony here is that Willis was considered a relatively enlightened practitioner.
sentences.zh: 这里残酷的讽刺在于，Willis 被认为是一位相对开明的从业者。

sentences.en: There were many institutions in England where the mentally ill were treated far, far worse: chained to walls, exhibited to the public, or simply left to rot in their own filth.
sentences.zh: 当时英格兰有许多机构，精神病患者在那里受到的待遇要糟糕得多：用铁链锁在墙上、向公众展示，或者任由他们在自己的污秽中腐烂。

sentences.en: Willis, at least, believed that patients could recover, and that this method was the most effective way of bringing about a recovery.
sentences.zh: 至少 Willis 相信患者是可以康复的，并且这种方法是实现康复的最有效途径。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, in Parliament, a crisis is unfolding.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在议会中，一场危机正在上演。

sentences.en: Parliament runs the day-to-day business of government.
sentences.zh: 议会负责政府的日常事务。

sentences.en: But many of the formal powers of the Crown, such as appointing ministers and giving royal assent to new laws, these require a functioning king.
sentences.zh: 但王权的许多法定权力，例如任命大臣和对新法律给予御准，这些都需要一个运转正常的国王。

sentences.en: Someone needs to exercise those powers in his place.
sentences.zh: 需要有人来代行这些权力。

sentences.en: The question of who that should be, and on what terms, consumes the House of Commons for months.
sentences.zh: 谁应该担任这个职位，以及在什么条件下担任，这些问题让下议院争论了好几个月。

sentences.en: Then George recovers, and the crisis becomes, for the moment, moot, irrelevant.
sentences.zh: 然后 George 康复了，这场危机暂时变得没有意义、无关紧要了。

sentences.en: By February of 1789, George begins to improve.
sentences.zh: 到 1789 年 2 月，George 开始好转。

sentences.en: By April, he is well enough to return to public life.
sentences.zh: 到了 4 月，他已经恢复到足以重返公众生活。

sentences.en: The recovery is met with national celebration.
sentences.zh: 他的康复迎来了全国性的庆祝。

sentences.en: Fireworks. Services of thanksgiving in churches across the country, and a grand ceremony at St Paul’s Cathedral.
sentences.zh: 烟花。全国各地教堂的感恩礼拜，以及在圣保罗大教堂举行的盛大仪式。

sentences.en: Farmer George, or rather King George, is back.
sentences.zh: 农民 George，或者更准确地说是 George 国王，回来了。

sentences.en: Sadly, it would not last. Further episodes followed, in 1801 and again in 1804, each one longer and more severe than the last.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，这并没有持续多久。随后在 1801 年和 1804 年又发生了发作，每一次都比前一次更长、更严重。

sentences.en: And then, in 1810, following the death of his youngest daughter, Princess Amelia, he began to decline for the final time.
sentences.zh: 然后，在 1810 年，在他最小的女儿阿米莉亚公主去世后，他的健康状况开始最后一次恶化。

sentences.en: By 1811, it was clear that he would not recover.
sentences.zh: 到 1811 年，很明显他不会康复了。

sentences.en: His eldest son, the future George IV, was appointed Prince Regent to govern in his place.
sentences.zh: 他的长子、未来的 George IV 被任命为摄政王代行统治。

sentences.en: George III was now confined to Windsor Castle.
sentences.zh: George III 此时已被禁锢在温莎城堡中。

sentences.en: By this point, he was old, blind, and partially deaf.
sentences.zh: 到了这个时候，他已经年迈、双目失明且部分失聪。

sentences.en: In his final years, his mind was gone entirely.
sentences.zh: 在他生命的最后几年里，他的神志完全丧失了。

sentences.en: He wandered the corridors at night, white-bearded and gaunt in his dressing gown, talking to people who had been dead for decades.
sentences.zh: 他穿着晨衣，顶着白胡子，面容憔悴，在夜间的走廊里徘徊，与那些已经死去几十年的人说话。

sentences.en: He lived like this for nine more years, before his death in 1820, aged eighty-one.
sentences.zh: 他以这种状态又生活了九年，直到 1820 年去世，享年八十一岁。

sentences.en: So, you might be asking yourself, what was actually wrong with him?
sentences.zh: 所以，你可能会问自己，他到底出了什么毛病？

sentences.en: This is the question that historians and doctors have been arguing about for more than a century.
sentences.zh: 这是历史学家和医生们争论了一个多世纪的问题。

sentences.en: For most of the twentieth century, the accepted answer was something called porphyria, specifically variegate porphyria, which is a hereditary blood disorder.
sentences.zh: 在整个二十世纪的大部分时间里，被普遍接受的答案是一种叫做卟啉症的疾病，具体来说是杂色卟啉症，这是一种遗传性血液疾病。

sentences.en: The theory was put forward in 1966 by two medical historians, who suggested that George's physical symptoms, such as discoloured urine and muscle weakness, these pointed to a metabolic disease rather than a psychiatric one.
sentences.zh: 这个理论是由两位医学历史学家在 1966 年提出的，他们认为 George 的身体症状（如尿液变色和肌肉无力）指向的是代谢性疾病，而不是精神疾病。

sentences.en: In other words, he wasn't a "madman"; this was a physical disease, not a mental illness.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他不是个“疯子”；这是一场身体上的疾病，而不是精神病。

sentences.en: The theory gained significant support in the early 2000s, when scientists analysed samples of George's hair and found arsenic at levels roughly a hundred times higher than those in healthy people.
sentences.zh: 这一理论在 2000 年代初得到了重大支持，当时科学家分析了 George 的头发样本，发现其中的砷含量大约是健康人的百倍左右。

sentences.en: The suggestion was that his doctors had been inadvertently poisoning him with arsenic -based medicines, which would have triggered and worsened any underlying condition.
sentences.zh: 大家的看法是，他的医生无意中用含砷药物毒害了他，这会引发并恶化任何潜在的病情。

sentences.en: But from around 2010 onwards, this theory began to fall apart.
sentences.zh: 但从 2010 年左右开始，这个理论开始瓦解。

sentences.en: A systematic review of George's actual medical records found that the two researchers had been highly selective.
sentences.zh: 对 George 实际病历的系统性审查发现，那两位研究人员进行了高度的选择性摘录。

sentences.en: They had emphasised the physical symptoms and quietly downplayed, or simply omitted, the psychiatric ones.
sentences.zh: 他们强调了身体症状，而悄悄淡化甚至直接忽略了精神症状。

sentences.en: The current consensus is that George III is likely to have had bipolar disorder.
sentences.zh: 目前的共识是，George III 很可能患有双相情感障碍。

sentences.en: Specifically, bipolar disorder type one, the kind characterised by full manic episodes.
sentences.zh: 具体来说是一型双相情感障碍，其特征是全面的躁狂发作。

sentences.en: The racing thoughts. The inability to stop speaking.
sentences.zh: 思维奔逸。无法停止说话。

sentences.en: The delusions. The grandiosity. The weeks of extreme agitation followed by periods of relative normality.
sentences.zh: 妄想。夸大狂。数周的极端狂躁，随之而来的是相对正常的时期。

sentences.en: These are not the symptoms of a blood disease; they are the hallmarks of severe mania.
sentences.zh: 这些都不是血液疾病的症状；它们是严重躁狂症的标志。

sentences.en: As for the arsenic levels in his hair, these were accurate.
sentences.zh: 至于他头发中的砷含量，这些都是准确的。

sentences.en: The finding was not exaggerated. But this was most probably a consequence of the treatments he received, rather than a cause of his illness.
sentences.zh: 这一发现并未夸大。但这很可能是他接受治疗的结果，而不是他生病的原因。

sentences.en: Today, as you may know, bipolar disorder is a condition that can be managed with medication and therapy, and many people with bipolar disorder type one lead full and productive lives.
sentences.zh: 如今，你可能知道，双相情感障碍是一种可以通过药物和心理治疗来控制的疾病，许多一型双相情感障碍患者过着充实且富有成效的生活。

sentences.en: But George had no such luxury. Instead, he was strapped into a jacket and chained to a chair.
sentences.zh: 但 George 没有这种奢侈的待遇。相反，他被穿上束衣，绑在椅子上。

sentences.en: And while the physicians might well have believed they were doing the right thing, indeed the only thing they could, they were almost certainly making it worse.
sentences.zh: 虽然医生们可能深信他们做的是对的事，甚至是他们唯一能做的事，但他们几乎肯定把病情弄得更糟了。

sentences.en: The bleeding, the purging, the blistering, these would have weakened him physically.
sentences.zh: 放血、泻药、起泡剂，这些都会在肉体上削弱他。

sentences.en: And the trauma of being restrained repeatedly, put into a straitjacket or tied to a chair, all this can hardly have calmed a mind already in crisis.
sentences.zh: 而一次次被束缚、被塞进束衣或被绑在椅子上的创伤，根本不可能让一个本就处于危机中的大脑平静下来。

sentences.en: It may well have intensified his fear, agitation and confusion, and triggered further manic episodes.
sentences.zh: 这很可能加剧了他的恐惧、焦虑和困惑，并引发了进一步的躁狂发作。

sentences.en: George III died on the 29th of January 1820 at Windsor Castle, aged eighty-one.
sentences.zh: George III 于 1820 年 1 月 29 日在温莎城堡逝世，享年八十一岁。

sentences.en: He had been king for fifty-nine years and ninety-six days.
sentences.zh: 他当了五十九年零九十六天的国王。

sentences.en: In that time, Britain had lost America, defeated Napoleon, expanded its empire across six continents, and begun the Industrial Revolution.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，英国失去了美洲，打败了拿破仑，将帝国扩展到六大洲，并开启了工业革命。

sentences.en: The world he left behind looked almost nothing like the world he had inherited.
sentences.zh: 他留下的世界与他继承的世界几乎毫无相似之处。

sentences.en: He had watched almost none of it. Not in the last decade, anyway.
sentences.zh: 这一切他几乎都没怎么见证。至少在最后十年里是没有的。

sentences.en: So, to wrap things up, the "mad king" remains one of history's most durable caricatures.
sentences.zh: 总之，归纳一下，“疯王”依然是历史上最具持久力的漫画式形象之一。

sentences.en: In American memory, he is a tyrant. In British popular culture, a figure of pity or of gentle comedy.
sentences.zh: 在美国人的记忆中，他是一个暴君。在英国大众文化中，他是一个令人同情或温和滑稽的人物。

sentences.en: The reality was neither tyranny nor romance.
sentences.zh: 现实既不是暴君，也不是传奇。

sentences.en: It was a conscientious, earnest, somewhat ordinary man, placed on the throne during an extraordinary age, and then crushed by an illness nobody around him had the tools to understand, let alone to treat.
sentences.zh: 他是一个恪尽职守、认真负责、甚至有些平凡的男人，被置于一个非凡的时代登上王位，然后被周围没有人有工具去理解、更不用说去治疗的疾病所摧毁。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on George III, the Mad King.
sentences.zh: 好了，关于 George III（疯王）的今日节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目很有趣，并且让你学到了新东西。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 一如既往，我很想知道你对这期节目有什么看法。

sentences.en: Let me know in the comments below, if you're listening to this somewhere where you can comment, and for the members among you, you can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 如果你在一个可以评论的地方听到这个，请在下方的评论区告诉我；对于我们当中的会员，你可以直接进入我们的社区论坛，网址是 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他好奇的头脑畅聊起来。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 推出的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，请注意安全，我们下期节目见。
